Each dot product still accumulates\n// k = 0..j-1 in ascending order, so the result is bit-identical to the sequential\n// row-oriented algorithm.\n\nbool choleskyDecomposition(std::vector<double>& A, const size_t n) {\n    // A is stored in row-major order\n    bool ok = true;\n\n    #pragma omp parallel\n    for (size_t j = 0; j < n; ++j) {\n        #pragma omp single\n        {\n            // Diagonal element\n            double sum = 0.0;\n            for (size_t k = 0; k < j; ++k) {\n                sum += A[j * n + k] * A[j * n + k];\n            }\n            const double val = A[j * n + j] - sum;\n            if (val <= 0.0) {\n                // Matrix is not positive definite\n                printf(\"Error: Matrix is not positive definite at diagonal element %zu\\n\", j);\n                ok = false;\n            } else {\n                A[j * n + j] = sqrt(val);\n            }\n        }\n        // The implicit barrier at the end of single makes ok consistent across threads\n        if (!ok) {\n            break;\n        }\n\n        // Off-diagonal elements of column j\n        #pragma omp for schedule(static)\n        for (size_t i = j + 1; {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011Cg1HEE7NBtAXoAKwkaMew","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The Cholesky benchmark now runs with OpenMP unconditionally, and it produces bit-identical results to the original.\n\n**Changes (only `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`):**\n- **Decomposition:** I changed the loop order from row-by-row to column-by-column. The `rand_r` loop stays sequential so the generated matrix is unchanged. The O(n²) error-reduction loop in validation stays sequential because it is cheap.\n- **Output:** I added one line, `OpenMP threads: N`, after the `Validation:` line so scaling runs can be interpreted. If an external parser expects the exact old line set, remove it.\n- **CMake:** `find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)` and `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX` are linked. Configuration fails if OpenMP is missing. The `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` flags and the `cholesky` target name are unchanged.\n\n**Why I kept bit-identical arithmetic:** each dot product still accumulates `k = 0..j-1` in ascending order. The `-r` output includes a hash, so an exact-match comparison is possible. Blocked or tiled variants would reorder the sums and change the low bits. I chose not to do that.\n\n**Verification:**\n- Build is clean with no warnings.\n- `-r` output (including the hash) matches the original build exactly for n = 1, 2, 3, 7, 64, 129, 512, and 1000.\n- `-v` passes at 512, 1024, and 2048 for every thread count tested.\n- Non-positive-definite input (checked in a scratch copy in /tmp) gives the same message and exit code as the original.\n\n**Timing (Cholesky step only, `-v` runs):**\n\n| n | 1 thread | 8 threads | 32 threads |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 512 | 29 ms (original 29 ms) | 7 ms | 5 ms |\n| 2048 | 2118 ms (original 2127 ms) | 289 ms | 102 ms |\n\nSingle-thread speed is unchanged. Scaling is near-linear up to about 32 threads and flattens at 64 threads on this 256-thread machine, where n = 512 is too small to keep the extra threads busy.\n\n**Not done:** I did not add row-level ILP (interleaving several rows per dot-product loop) or cache blocking.
